cao--america.description: Introduced in 2007, CAO America is built with two wrapper leaves, Connecticut Broadleaf and Connecticut Shade, rolled into a fine pinstripe over a Brazilian binder and a filler of Nicaraguan, Dominican, Italian and American tobacco. It starts sweet and peppery, then settles into earth and a steady leather note, a measured smoke for an unhurried afternoon.

cao--amazon-basin.description: The first of CAO's Amazon releases, launched in 2014 at STG Estelí: an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper and Nicaraguan binder around a filler that is roughly forty percent Bragança, a Brazilian leaf from the Amazon that is rolled into tubes and fermented naturally for six months. The smoke is woody and leathery, with dark chocolate, espresso and a faint smokiness.

thirds.notes: Earth, leather and dark chocolate with nuts and oak, and a lively pepper through the nose.
Leather takes the lead over oak, cocoa and bitter espresso, with a light smokiness and a cinnamon-sugar sweetness.
Leather, espresso and oak remain with a touch of earth; the last inches can turn bitter.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – CAO Orellana now shipping

cao--amazon-basin-extra-anejo.description: A limited Amazon Basin toro with the original recipe idea: Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, Nicaraguan binder and a filler of Dominican and Colombian leaf with Amazonian Bragança, made in Nicaragua and rested for two years before release. The extra age gives a smooth, mellow smoke of cedar and cream with a light spice.

thirds.notes: A soft start with a hint of spice, soon joined by light cedar and cream.
Cedar becomes clearer while the smoke stays notably mellow.
The cedar eases a little and the smoke stays smooth and creamy to the end.

sources.title: Cigar Czars – CAO Amazon Basin Extra Añejo review
JR Cigars – CAO Amazon Basin Extra Añejo

cao--orellana.description: The fourth Amazon release, shipped in 2019 as a limited 6 x 52 toro from STG Estelí. A sun-grown Brazilian Cubra wrapper from Bahia, aged more than five years, covers a Nicaraguan binder and a filler of Colombian, Dominican and Brazilian Bragança tobacco, with a band that runs down the cigar in a barber-pole spiral.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – CAO Orellana now shipping
Blind Man's Puff – Quick review CAO Orellana

thirds.notes: White pepper, oak and earth, with dried cherry and a floral, slightly mineral edge.
Woody and earthy with coffee and cinnamon-like spice; a mineral note softens the retrohale.
Oak and kitchen spices over coffee, with pepper on the retrohale and some bitterness at the end.

cao--fuma-em-corda.description: Released in 2017 as part of CAO's Amazon trilogy, this blend uses a Honduran oscuro wrapper, a Cameroon binder and a filler of Nicaraguan and Honduran leaf with Brazilian Fuma em Corda, rope-cured tobacco. A smokeable cord is wound around the head. Expect espresso and earth with dried fruit, cedar and toasted nuts, turning tangier as it burns.

thirds.notes: Espresso and earth with a candied-fruit sweetness, then cedar, savoury spice and a floral, nutty aroma.
A lemon-peel edge brings slight bitterness before toasted nuts and a spicier aroma appear.
Burning through the rope, the smoke turns tangy and fruity with a cooling, minty touch near the end.

sources.title: Stogie Press – CAO Fuma em Corda review
Cigar Dojo – CAO Fuma em Corda Robusto

cao--arcana.description: A limited CAO series, begun in 2021 at STG Estelí, that looks at old fermentation methods. The first release, Mortal Coil, wraps Connecticut Broadleaf over a Connecticut Shade binder and a filler built around Dominican andullo, leaf fermented for about two years bound in palm, with Honduran, Nicaraguan and Dominican tobacco. Later editions follow the same idea with other traditions.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – CAO launches Arcana series with Mortal Coil
Blind Man's Puff – CAO announces Arcana series

cao--bones.description: A Connecticut-led blend created by CAO's Rick Rodriguez as a nod to dominoes and dice games: a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper and Connecticut Shade binder over Dominican, Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. The smoke is soft and creamy, moving from cedar and a touch of white pepper to earth, unsweetened cocoa and baking spice.

thirds.notes: Cedar and a graham-cracker sweetness with a little white pepper.
Creamy earth with bread, unsweetened cocoa and baking spice; the smoke stays light.
Heavy cream, earth and more cocoa, with a spicy cedar on a clean finish.

sources.title: Best Cigar Prices – CAO Bones review

cao--brazilia.description: One of CAO's long-standing regional blends, finished in a dark, oily Brazilian wrapper. It opens with deep earth, wood and black pepper, then shows hints of stone fruit before cinnamon, caramel and smoky hickory take over in the last third. A dark, slightly sweet cigar for after dinner.

thirds.notes: Deep earth and wood with a black pepper that lingers on the palate.
Muted peach and apple appear through the nose while pepper and rich tobacco stay in front.
Cinnamon and caramel come forward, then hickory, with the cinnamon softening to nutmeg.

cao--bx3.description: Made in Nicaragua and launched in 2022, BX3 stands for Brazil times three: a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper and Arapiraca binder, with Brazilian leaf joining Honduran, Mexican and Nicaraguan tobacco in the filler. It starts with chili-like pepper over earth and dry wood, then turns to coffee, cocoa and Brazil nut, finishing dark and sticky.

thirds.notes: Red and black pepper heat over earth, dry wood and leather, with dried fruit, cocoa nibs and coffee bean.
Floral and tea-like notes on the retrohale, clearer coffee and cocoa, and a milky Brazil-nut sweetness.
Dark, chewy and sticky, with nutty chocolate and leather as body and spice build.

sources.title: Stogie Press – CAO BX3 Robusto review

cao--cameroon.description: Created to mark CAO's thirtieth year, this line puts an oily, nut-brown African Cameroon wrapper over a Nicaraguan long filler. It is a balanced, gently sweet smoke with light coffee and the soft spice typical of Cameroon leaf, suited to a relaxed hour.

sources.title: Mike's Cigars – CAO Cameroon Robusto review

cao--colombia.description: Made at STG Estelí, CAO Colombia pairs a Honduran wrapper from the Jamastran valley and a Cameroon binder with Colombian filler and Brazilian Mata Fina. It is a gentle, sweet smoke of hay, honey and tea, with an earthy, slightly musky middle that recalls a peaty whisky on the retrohale.

thirds.notes: Hay and grass with sweet tea and honey, and a slight tingle on the tongue.
The Colombian filler shows as earthy musk, with a peaty note on the retrohale.
Sweet tea, honey and soft musk carry through without major change.

cao--consigliere.description: Shown in 2016 and made at STG Estelí, Consigliere carries the recipe of CAO's 2005 Sopranos cigar: a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper, a Honduran binder and filler from Colombia, the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. It brings sweetened coffee, cocoa and leather with sharp pepper on the retrohale, moving to espresso, hardwood and cinnamon.

thirds.notes: Sweetened medium-roast coffee, cocoa powder and leather over minerals, with red and black pepper on the retrohale.
Espresso, dry hardwood and earth with warm cinnamon, and a sharper black pepper through the nose.
Sweetness recedes, leaving natural tobacco, hardwood and leather with heavy smoke.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – CAO Consigliere Associate review
Cigar Dojo – CAO unveils Consigliere at IPCPR 2016

cao--fasa-sol.description: Launched in 2024 and rolled at the HATSA factory in Honduras, FASA Sol uses a Honduran Olancho San Agustín wrapper and a Cameroon binder over Dominican filler and leaf from three Nicaraguan regions. Black coffee and leather run through it, framed by pear-like fruit, brown sugar and black pepper.

thirds.notes: Pear and apple with light brown sugar over leathery black coffee and black pepper.
The leathery coffee grows while the sweet notes fade.
Fruit and brown sugar return and soften the coffee towards the finish.

sources.title: Tiny Tim's Blog – CAO FASA Sol Toro
Cigar Czars – CAO FASA Sol and Noche review

cao--flathead.description: Introduced in 2013 at STG Estelí, Flathead is CAO's hot-rod line, box-pressed and finished with a flattened head, with sizes named after engine parts. A Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper and Connecticut Habano binder hold Nicaraguan ligero and Dominican Piloto Cubano. It is strong from the start, with spice, cedar, cream and earth giving way to espresso and sugarcane.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – CAO Flathead V660 Carb review
Stogie Press – CAO Flathead V660 Carb review
Cigar Inspector – CAO Flathead V660 Carb

thirds.notes: Red pepper and cocoa with a natural sweetness, then a creamy coffee smoke.
Chocolate, leather and cream grow bolder, with a molasses-like sweetness and some cedar.
Cocoa and cream with coffee bean and cedar; strength starts to build and the finish is long.

cao--flathead-speed-shop.description: A newer, milder branch of the Flathead family, available from 2026, that keeps the box-pressed hot-rod format. It uses an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper and a Mexican San Andrés binder over Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. Leather leads from start to finish in a medium-bodied smoke.

sources.title: Cigar Czars – CAO Speed Shop review

cao--flathead-steel-horse.description: Launched in 2015 at STG Estelí, Steel Horse brings the Flathead idea to motorcycle culture with its own blend: a Connecticut Habano grueso wrapper, a Brazilian Arapiraca binder and filler from the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Nicaragua. Earth, oak, leather and dark chocolate lead, with a hint of vanilla and a creamy cedar finish.

thirds.notes: Earth, oak, leather and dark chocolate with a little vanilla sweetness and black pepper on the retrohale.
The profile blurs for a while as the finish turns creamier and strength rises.
Creamy cedar and dark chocolate return in focus, with gritty earth, leather, nuts and hay.

sources.title: halfwheel – CAO Flathead Steel Horse Apehanger review
Klaro Cigars – CAO Flathead Steel Horse review

cao--flavours.description: CAO's family of infused cigars and cigarillos, rolled with Cameroon wrapper on the classic Moontrance and long-filler tobacco throughout. Each variant has its own infusion: Madagascar vanilla for Bella Vanilla, orange-blossom honey for Gold Honey, Irish whiskey and cream for Eileen's Dream, cherry and black currant for Cherrybomb, fruit and bourbon vanilla for Moontrance.

sources.title: Cigar World – Deep dive: CAO Flavours

cao--gold.description: A gentle CAO blend with a light Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler. The smoke is woody and creamy, with hints of orange peel, almond and raisin, an easy choice for a morning or a first cigar of the day.

thirds.notes: Creamy and mellow: natural tobacco with a faint pie-like spice, then wood and some nuttiness.
Wood leads over a nutty background, and the spice returns.
Nuttiness takes over, with wood and spice; the smoke stays cool and mellow.

cao--italia.description: A Nicaraguan-made CAO blend that pays tribute to Italy: Honduran wrapper and binder over a filler that includes Italian-grown tobacco alongside Nicaraguan and Peruvian leaf. The Italian and Peruvian tobacco gives an unusual earthiness, with cocoa and coffee notes in a medium-full smoke.

cao--mx2.description: MX2 is built around two layers of maduro leaf: a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper with a dark Brazilian leaf beneath it, over a filler of Dominican, Honduran, Nicaraguan and Peruvian tobacco, made in Nicaragua. It delivers dark chocolate and coffee with an earthy sweetness, then cocoa and leather, growing richer and stronger towards the end.

thirds.notes: Bold dark chocolate and coffee with an earthy sweetness.
Cocoa and leather with a sweetness that is hard to place.
Bolder and richer, with strength rising noticeably but without harshness.

cao--nicaragua.description: A Nicaraguan-made CAO blend with Honduran wrapper and binder around a Nicaraguan filler, the sizes named after Nicaraguan towns. It opens with strong earth, pepper and spice, then turns creamier with coffee and a maple-like sweetness and a campfire note, before the pepper returns for a full finish.

thirds.notes: A strong earthy Nicaraguan opening with pepper and spice, burning slowly.
Creamier, with coffee in front, a maple-like sweetness and a campfire edge.
The pepper returns and the smoke feels full, with little further change.

sources.title: Cigar Place – CAO Nicaragua Tipitapa review

cao--osa-sol.description: The first CAO release after the move to General Cigar, built around a wrapper from Olancho San Agustín, a fertile Honduran valley, over a Connecticut binder and Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. It starts spicy and dry, then shows wood and citrus as the spice fades, a lively, fresh-tasting cigar.

thirds.notes: Pronounced pepper on palate and throat, with a dry edge and a hint of cedar and citrus.
Citrus begins to show beside the wood while the spice fades.
Spice has nearly gone; wood and citrus lead to the finish.

sources.title: Half Ashed – CAO OSA Sol Lot 50 review

cao--pilon.description: Released in 2015 from STG Estelí, Pilón takes its name from a 19th-century Cuban way of fermenting tobacco in small round piles, which works slowly and lowers ammonia in the leaf. An Ecuadorian Habano wrapper covers a Nicaraguan binder and filler. Dry earth, wood and cocoa open, and pepper grows into a bold, earthy finish.

thirds.notes: Dry earth, pepper, sweet wood and milk chocolate, with mostly cocoa on the retrohale.
Pepper settles on the palate as the wrapper's earth and wood take over and strength rises.
The boldest part: pepper dominates and adds depth to the earth while the wood recedes.

cao--pilon-anejo.description: An aged version of Pilón, first released in limited numbers in 2022 and later made permanent. Rolled in Honduras with an Ecuadorian-grown Cuban-seed Sumatra wrapper, a Honduran Habano binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler with ligero, it rests about two years after rolling. Molasses, cedar and spice build to leather, malt and dried dates.

thirds.notes: A rough, earthy start smooths into wrapper spice, molasses and growing cedar.
Honduran earth comes forward with malted milk, leather and candied dates.
Molasses, leather, granola and dried dates intensify into a tangy, chewy finish.

sources.title: Klaro Cigars – CAO Pilón Añejo review
Tiny Tim's Blog – CAO Pilón Añejo Robusto

cao--session.description: Released in 2019, Session is CAO's laid-back cigar, with a band that tells the smoker to sit, smoke and chill. A Connecticut Broadleaf maduro wrapper and Dominican binder hold Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. It starts sweet and peppery, then settles into nuts and wood with gentle spice, holding its flavour to the end.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – CAO Session Garage

thirds.notes: Pepper with raisin, roasted hazelnut and toasted bread, over an earthy, slightly herbal base.
Chocolate malt and dark coffee with oak, a mineral note and a peppery retrohale.
Stewed plum and cedar with coffee and cinnamon-like spice, ending on a bitter, peppery edge.

cao--vision.description: Vision first appeared in 2007 in a box lit with blue LEDs; CAO revived the name in 2020 with a new limited blend by Rick Rodriguez, his first with Cameroon wrapper. An Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and Nicaraguan Habano filler from Estelí and Jalapa sit beneath it. Cedar, nougat, honey and toast lead, with peanut, coffee and cinnamon later.

thirds.notes: Minerals, white chocolate and raisin, then cedar, nougat, toasted bread and honey.
Cedar, nougat and honey remain, joined by roasted peanuts and a mild creamy coffee.
Cinnamon arrives as the sweetness fades, leaving toast, black pepper and mild coffee.

cao--zocalo.description: CAO's first cigar with a Mexican wrapper, named after Mexico City's main square and released in 2018 from STG Estelí. A San Andrés Morrón wrapper covers a Cameroon binder and Nicaraguan filler. It opens with cedar and a whiskey-like sweetness, turns earthy with layered pepper and leather, and finishes dense and bready.

thirds.notes: Cedar with a whiskey-like sweetness and ripe fruit, then orange, florals and earth.
Much earthier, with white, green and black pepper and leather on the retrohale.
Still earthy and bready, the pepper reduced but lasting on the finish.
